applies_to: Verasys BYP200 bypass damper controllers that hold duct static pressure in a zoning system.
summary: The BYP200 modulates a bypass damper to hold duct static pressure in a Verasys zoning system. Through the SBH it exposes 7 objects: duct static pressure and setpoint, maximum damper position, damper output, heating/cooling mode, zone occupancy and unit enable.
notes: Object names are the short Verasys names as printed. The guide gives no units or state texts; multistate state texts come from the device.
Access is from the Writable column (TRUE = writable).

source.title: Verasys BACnet over IP Integration User Guide

integration.summary: Integrate through the Verasys Smart Building Hub: enable BACnet routing on the SBH, and the supervisor then sees each system bus device behind the SBH's MS/TP network. Map the enable and occupancy commands, the main setpoints and the status and alarm points.
setup: Devices on the Verasys system bus are reached through the Smart Building Hub (SBH, LC-SBH200/300) BACnet routing feature; the SBH needs a wired Ethernet connection (its Wi-Fi client does not route BACnet IP).

In SBH Settings > BACnet Settings: MS/TP device object identifier (default 1), MAC (default 117) and MS/TP network number (default 64,999); set Routing Mode to Enabled, UDP port (default 47808) and IP network number (default 1,001).
If the SBH and the supervisor are on different IP subnets, set up BBMD entries on both (SBH Settings > BBMD).
SBH schedules become visible to the supervisor; only Occupied/Unoccupied and On/Off schedules are supported.
gotchas: The SBH routes BACnet IP only over Ethernet, not Wi-Fi.
Give every system bus device a unique device object identifier on the BACnet network.
